text: Let y = y(x) be a solution curve of the differential equation $(y+1)\tan ^{2}xdx+\tan xdy+ydx=0$, $x\in \left (0,\frac{π}{2}\right )$. If $\lim _{x\to 0+}xy(x)=1$, then the value of $y\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(y+1)\tan ^{2}xdx+\tan xdy+ydx=0$

or $\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{\sec ^{2}x}{\tan x}.y=-\tan x$

$IF=e^{\int \frac{\sec 2x}{\tan x}dx}=e^{\ln \tan x}=\tan x$

$\therefore$ $y\tan x=-\int \tan ^{2}xdx$

or $y\tan x=-\tan x+x+C$

or $y=-1+\frac{x}{\tan x}+\frac{C}{\tan x}$

or $\lim _{x\to 0}xy=-x+\frac{x^{2}}{\tan x}+\frac{Cx}{\tan x}=1$

or C = 1

$y(x)=\cot x+x\cot x-1$

$y\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=\frac{π}{4}$

text: Let A and B be independent events such that P(A) = p, P(B) = 2p. The largest value of p, for which P (exactly one of A, B occurs) = $\frac{5}{9}$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
P (Exactly one of A or B)

$=P\left (A\cap B–\right )+\left (A–\cap B\right )=\frac{5}{9}$

$=P(A)P(B–)+P(A–)P(B)=\frac{5}{9}$

$\Rightarrow P(A)(1-P(B))+(1-P(A))P(B)=\frac{5}{9}$

$\Rightarrow p(1-2p)+(1-p)2p=\frac{5}{9}$

$\Rightarrow 36p^{2}-27p+5=0$

$\Rightarrow p=\frac{1}{3}$ or $\frac{5}{12}$

$p_{\max }=\frac{5}{12}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift

text: Out of all the patients in a hospital 89% are found to be suffering from heart ailment and 98% are suffering from lungs infection. If K% of them are suffering from both ailments, then K can not belong to the set :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
This solution begins by applying the principle of inclusion and exclusion, which in the context of this problem, is represented by the formula : 

n(A ∪ B) ≥ n(A) + n(B) - n(A ∩ B)

Here, n(A ∪ B) represents the total number of patients in the hospital, which is 100%. n(A) represents the proportion of patients with a heart ailment (89%), and n(B) represents the proportion of patients with a lung infection (98%). 

By rearranging this formula, the solution establishes an inequality for n(A ∩ B), the proportion of patients suffering from both ailments :

100% ≥ 89% + 98% - n(A ∩ B)

Therefore, 

n(A ∩ B) ≥ 87%

Next, the solution notes that n(A ∩ B) cannot be greater than the smaller of n(A) and n(B), since it cannot be larger than the smallest group. Thus, we have another inequality :

n(A ∩ B) ≤ 89%

Combining these two inequalities gives :

87% ≤ n(A ∩ B) ≤ 89%

Hence, the proportion of patients suffering from both ailments must be a value between 87% and 89% inclusive. So, the set of values {79,81,83,85} which are all less than 87% are values that n(A ∩ B) cannot belong to. Therefore, option C is the correct answer.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift

text: The value of $\int\limits _{\frac{-1}{\sqrt{2}}}^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left (\left (\frac{x+1}{x-1}\right )^{2}+\left (\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right )^{2}-2\right )^{\frac{1}{2}}dx$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\sqrt{\left (\frac{x+1}{x-1}\right )^{2}+\left (\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right )^{2}-2}$

$=\sqrt{\left (\frac{x+1}{x-1}-\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right )^{2}}$

$=\left |\frac{x+1}{x-1}-\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right |$

$=\left |\frac{(x+1)^{2}-(x-1)^{2}}{x^{2}-1}\right |$

$=\left |\frac{x^{2}+2x+1-x^{2}+2x-1}{x^{2}-1}\right |$

$=\left |\frac{4x}{x^{2}-1}\right |$

$\therefore$ $I=\int\limits _{-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left [\left (\frac{x+1}{x-1}\right )^{2}+\left (\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right )^{2}-2\right ]^{\frac{1}{2}}dx$

$I=\int\limits _{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left |\frac{4x}{x^{2}-1}\right |dx$

Let $f(x)=\left |\frac{4x}{x^{2}-1}\right |$

$\therefore$ $f(-x)=\left |\frac{4(-x)}{(-x)^{2}-1}\right |=\left |\frac{-4x}{x^{2}-1}\right |=\left |\frac{4x}{x^{2}-1}\right |$

$\Rightarrow f(x)=f(-x)$

$\therefore$ f(x) is a even function.

$\therefore$ $I=2\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\left |\frac{4x}{x^{2}-1}\right |dx$

Using property, If f(x) is an even function then,

$\int\limits _{-a}^{a}f(x)=2\int\limits _{0}^{a}f(x)dx$

x > 0 when $x\in \left [0,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{2} > 0$ when $x\in \left [0,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{2}$ $-$ 1 < 0 when $x\in \left [0,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{x^{2}-1}<0$ when $x\in \left [0,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow \frac{4x}{x^{2}-1}<0$ when $x\in \left [0,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right ]$

$\therefore$ $\left |\frac{4x}{x^{2}-1}\right |=-\frac{4x}{x^{2}-1}$ when $x\in \left [0,\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right ]$

$\therefore$ $I=2\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}-\left (\frac{4x}{x^{2}-1}\right )dx$

$=-4\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}\frac{2x}{x^{2}-1}dx$

$=-4\left [\log _{e}\left |x^{2}-1\right |\right ]_{0}^{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}$

$=-4\left [\log \left |\frac{1}{2}-1\right |-\log |-1|\right ]$

$=-4\log _{e}\left |-\frac{1}{2}\right |$

$=-4\log _{e}\frac{1}{2}$

$=-4\log _{e}^{2^{-1}}$

$=4\log _{e}^{2}$

$=\log _{e}^{2^{4}}$

$=\log _{e}^{16}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift

text: If $A=⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{ll} \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{-2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \end{array}⎞⎠⎟$, $B=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ i & 1 \end{array}\right )$, $i=\sqrt{-1}$, and $Q = A^{T}BA$, then the inverse of the matrix $A Q^{2021} A^{T}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$AA^{T}=⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{ll} \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{-2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \end{array}⎞⎠⎟⎛⎝⎜\begin{array}{ll} \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{-2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \end{array}⎞⎠⎟$

$AA^{T}=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right )=I$

$Q^{2}=A^{T}BAA^{T}BA=A^{T}BIBA$

$\Rightarrow Q^{2}=A^{T}B^{2}A$

$Q^{3}=A^{T}B^{2}AA^{T}BA\Rightarrow Q^{3}=A^{T}B^{3}A$

Similarly : $Q^{2021}=A^{T}B^{2021}A$

Now, $B^{2}=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ i & 1 \end{array}\right )\left (\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ i & 1 \end{array}\right )=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 2i & 1 \end{array}\right )$

$B^{3}=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 2i & 1 \end{array}\right )\left (\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ i & 1 \end{array}\right )\Rightarrow B^{3}=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 3i & 1 \end{array}\right )$

Similarly $B^{2021}=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 2021i & 1 \end{array}\right )$

$\therefore$ $AQ^{2021}A^{T}=AA^{T}B^{2021}AA^{T}=IB^{2021}I$

$\Rightarrow AQ^{2021}A^{T}=B^{2021}=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 2021i & 1 \end{array}\right )$

$\therefore$ $(AQ^{2021}A^{T})^{-1}=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 2021i & 1 \end{array}\right )^{-1}=\left (\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ -2021i & 1 \end{array}\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift

text: If the sum of an infinite $GP a, ar, ar^{2}, ar^{3}$, ....... is 15 and the sum of the squares of its each term is 150, then the sum of $ar^{2}, ar^{4}, ar^{6}$, ....... is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Sum of infinite terms :

$\frac{a}{1-r}=15$ ..... (i)

Series formed by square of terms :

$a^{2}, a^{2}r^{2}, a^{2}r^{4}, a^{2}r^{6}$ .......

Sum = $\frac{a^{2}}{1-r^{2}}=150$

$\Rightarrow \frac{a}{1-r}.\frac{a}{1+r}=150\Rightarrow 15.\frac{a}{1+r}=150$

$\Rightarrow \frac{a}{1+r}=10$ ...... (ii)

by (i) and (ii), a = 12; r = $\frac{1}{5}$

Now, series : $ar^{2}, ar^{4}, ar^{6}$

Sum = $\frac{ar^{2}}{1-r^{2}}=\frac{12.\left (\frac{1}{25}\right )}{1-\frac{1}{25}}=\frac{1}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift

text: Let $z=\frac{1-i\sqrt{3}}{2}$, $i=\sqrt{-1}$. Then the value of $21+\left (z+\frac{1}{z}\right )^{3}+\left (z^{2}+\frac{1}{z^{2}}\right )^{3}+\left (z^{3}+\frac{1}{z^{3}}\right )^{3}+....+\left (z^{21}+\frac{1}{z^{21}}\right )^{3}$ is $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$z=\frac{1-i\sqrt{3}}{2}=e^{-i\frac{π}{3}}$

$z^{r}+\frac{1}{z^{r}}=2\cos \left (-\frac{π}{3}\right )r=2\cos \frac{rπ}{3}$

$\Rightarrow 21+\sum\limits _{r=1}^{21}\left (z^{r}+\frac{1}{z^{r}}\right )^{3}=8\left (\cos ^{3}\frac{rπ}{3}\right )=2\left (\cos rπ+3\cos \frac{rπ}{3}\right )$

$\Rightarrow 21+\left (z+\frac{1}{z}\right )^{3}+\left (z^{2}+\frac{1}{z^{2}}\right )^{3}+....\left (z^{21}+\frac{1}{z^{21}}\right )^{3}$

$=21+\sum\limits _{r=1}^{21}\left (z^{r}+\frac{1}{z^{r}}\right )^{3}$

$=21+\sum\limits _{r=1}^{21}\left (2\cos rπ+6\cos \frac{rπ}{3}\right )$

$=21-2-6$

$=13$

text: The sum of all integral values of k (k $\neq$ 0) for which the equation $\frac{2}{x-1}-\frac{1}{x-2}=\frac{2}{k}$ in x has no real roots, is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{2}{x-1}-\frac{1}{x-2}=\frac{2}{k}$

$x\in R-\{1,2\}$

$\Rightarrow k(2x-4-x+1)=2(x^{2}-3x+2)$

$\Rightarrow k(x-3)=2(x^{2}-3x+2)$

for x $\neq$ 3, $k=2\left (x-3+\frac{2}{x-3}+3\right )$

$x-3+\frac{2}{x-3}\geq 2\sqrt{2},\forall x>3$

& $x-3+\frac{2}{x-3}\leq -2\sqrt{2},\forall x<-3$

$\Rightarrow 2\left (x-3+\frac{2}{x-3}+3\right )\in \left (-\infty ,6-4\sqrt{2}\right ]\cup \left [6+4\sqrt{2},\infty \right )$

for no real roots

$k\in (6-4\sqrt{2},6+4\sqrt{2})-\{0\}$

Integral k$\in${1, 2 ..... 11}

Sum of k = 66

text: A wire of length 36 m is cut into two pieces, one of the pieces is bent to form a square and the other is bent to form a circle. If the sum of the areas of the two figures is minimum, and the circumference of the circle is k (meter), then $\left (\frac{4}{π}+1\right )k$ is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let x + y = 36

x is perimeter of square and y is perimeter of circle side of square = x/4

radius of circle = $\frac{y}{2π}$

Sum Areas = $\left (\frac{x}{4}\right )^{2}+π\left (\frac{y}{2π}\right )^{2}$

$=\frac{x^{2}}{16}+\frac{(36-x)^{2}}{4π}$

For min Area :

$x=\frac{144}{π+4}$

$\Rightarrow$ Radius = y = 36 $-$ $\frac{144}{π+4}$

$\Rightarrow$ k = $\frac{36π}{π+4}$

$\left (\frac{4}{π}+1\right )k$ = 36

text: If y = y(x) is an implicit function of x such that $\log _{e}(x + y) = 4xy$, then $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}$ at x = 0 is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
ln(x + y) = 4xy (At x = 0, y = 1)

$x + y = e^{4xy}$

$\Rightarrow 1+\frac{dy}{dx}=e^{4xy}\left (4x\frac{dy}{dx}+4y\right )$

At x = 0 

$\frac{dy}{dx}=3$

At x = 0, $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}=e^{0}(4)^{2}+e^{0}(24)$

$\Rightarrow \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}=40$

text:
Let a, b $\in$ R, b $\neq$ 0, Define a function 

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} a\sin \frac{π}{2}(x-1), & forx\leq 0 \\ \frac{\tan 2x-\sin 2x}{bx^{3}}, & forx>0 \end{array} \right.$. 

If f is continuous at x = 0, then 10 $-$ ab is equal to $________________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} a\sin \frac{π}{2}(x-1), & forx\leq 0 \\ \frac{\tan 2x-\sin 2x}{bx^{3}}, & forx>0 \end{array} \right.$

For continuity at '0'

$\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}f(x)=f(0)$

$\Rightarrow \lim _{x\to 0^{+}}\frac{\tan 2x-\sin 2x}{bx^{3}}=-a$

$\Rightarrow \lim _{x\to 0^{+}}\frac{\frac{8x3}{3}+\frac{8x3}{3!}}{bx^{3}}=-a$

$\Rightarrow 8\left (\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3!}\right )=-ab$

$\Rightarrow 4=-ab$

$\Rightarrow 10-ab=14$
